title: Integrated molecular modeling and dynamics approaches revealed potential natural inhibitors of NF-kappaB transcription factor as breast cancer therapeutics.
authors: Zubair, Muhammad; Khalil, Sidra; Rasul, Ijaz; Nadeem, Habibullah; Noor, Fatima; Ahmad, Sajjad; Alrumaihi, Faris; Allemailem, Khaled S; Almatroudi, Ahmad; Alshehri, Faez Falah; Alshehri, Zafer Saad
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选NF-kappaB转录因子的小分子抑制剂，虽涉及TF-DNA相关蛋白，但聚焦药物发现而非TF-DNA结合机制，方法可迁移但对象和互作轴匹配度中等。
abstract: Breast cancer is a silent killer malady among women and a serious economic burden in health care management. A case of breast cancer is diagnosed among women every 19 s, and every 74 s, a woman dies of breast cancer somewhere in the world. Despite the pop-up of progressive research, advanced treatment approaches, and preventive measures, breast cancer remains amplifying ailment. The nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB) is a key transcription factor that links inflammation with cancer and is demonstrated as being involved in the tumorigenesis of breast cancer. The NF-kappaB transcription factor family in mammals consists of five proteins; c-Rel, RelA(p65), RelB, NF-kappaB1(p50), and NF-kappaB2(p52). The antitumor effect of NF-kappaB has also been explored in breast cancer, however, the actual treatment for breast cancer is yet to be discovered. This study is attributed to the identification of novel drug targets against breast cancer by targeting c-Rel, RelA(p65), RelB, NF-kappaB1(p50), and NF-kappaB2(p52) proteins. To identify the putative active compounds, a structure-based 3D pharmacophore model to the protein active site cavity was generated followed by virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. Initially, a library of 45000 compounds were docked against the target protein and five compounds namely Z56811101, Z653426226, Z1097341967, Z92743432, and Z464101066 were selected for further analysis. The relative binding affinity of Z56811101, Z653426226, Z1097341967, Z92743432, and Z464101066 with NF-kappaB1 (p50), NF-kappaB2 (p52), RelA (p65), RelB, and c-Rel proteins were -6.8, -8, -7.0, -6.9, and -7.2 kcal/mol, respectively which remained stable throughout the simulations of 200 ns. Furthermore, all of these compounds depict maximum drug-like properties. Therefore, the proposed compounds can be a potential candidate for patients with breast cancer, but, experimental validation is needed to ensure their safety.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 乳腺癌是女性中的一种无声杀手疾病，也是医疗管理中的重大经济负担。每19秒就有一例乳腺癌在女性中被诊断出来，而每74秒，世界上就有一名女性死于乳腺癌。尽管出现了进步性研究、先进治疗方法和预防措施，乳腺癌仍然是不断扩大的疾病。核因子kappa B（NF-kappaB）是将炎症与癌症联系起来的关键转录因子，并已被证明参与乳腺癌的肿瘤发生。哺乳动物中的NF-kappaB转录因子家族由五种蛋白质组成：c-Rel、RelA(p65)、RelB、NF-kappaB1(p50)和NF-kappaB2(p52)。NF-kappaB的抗肿瘤作用也已在乳腺癌中进行了探索，然而，乳腺癌的实际治疗方法尚未被发现。本研究旨在通过靶向c-Rel、RelA(p65)、RelB、NF-kappaB1(p50)和NF-kappaB2(p52)蛋白，识别针对乳腺癌的新型药物靶点。为了识别推定活性化合物，生成了基于结构的3D药效团模型，针对蛋白质活性位点空腔，随后进行了虚拟筛选、分子对接和分子动力学（MD）模拟。最初，将45000种化合物的库对靶蛋白进行对接，并选择了五种化合物，即Z56811101、Z653426226、Z1097341967、Z92743432和Z464101066，用于进一步分析。Z56811101、Z653426226、Z1097341967、Z92743432和Z464101066与NF-kappaB1(p50)、NF-kappaB2(p52)、RelA(p65)、RelB和c-Rel蛋白的相对结合亲和力分别为-6.8、-8、-7.0、-6.9和-7.2 kcal/mol，这些值在200 ns的模拟过程中保持稳定。此外，所有这些化合物都表现出最大的药物样特性。因此，所提出的化合物可能成为乳腺癌患者的潜在候选药物，但需要实验验证以确保其安全性。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
